summary: Ten comment-endorsed picks: terminal interfaces, local AI, home media, and interactive learning.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Ratatui
items.source_story_title: Terminal borders that don't cost a cell
items.summary: Rust library for terminal interfaces, praised by a former Alacritty maintainer.
items.why_included: A terminal maintainer explicitly endorses the library while using it for Markdown rendering.
items.evidence: A former Alacritty maintainer says they love Ratatui and are building ratmark, while noting a need for link support.

evidence_sources.author: nixpulvis
evidence_sources.excerpt: BTW, love ratatui. I've been building ratmark lately, for markdown rendering. But I really need link support ;)

items.name: llama.cpp
items.summary: Local inference engine; a CPU-only user praises speed gains from upgrades.
items.why_included: Resurfaced after the cooldown for specific long-term CPU-use evidence rather than a release headline.
items.evidence: A user running llama.cpp on a CPU-only machine for over a year praises performance improvements from upgrades.

evidence_sources.author: owlmem
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been running llama.cpp on a plain CPU-only box for local work for over a year now, and the thing that keeps surprising me is how often an upgrade is just free performance.

items.name: DeepSeek V3 JAX
items.source_story_title: Show HN: DeepSeek V3 in ~200 lines of pure Jax
items.summary: Compact DeepSeek architecture implementation; a Radeon user reports successful end-to-end training.
items.why_included: Independent hands-on success makes this more than a creator's educational demo.
items.evidence: A Fedora user calls the project their first successful end-to-end training run on an RX 7600 XT and welcomes the starting point.

evidence_sources.author: joebarbere
evidence_sources.excerpt: Thanks for this! I've been trying to get local training working on Fedora with ROCm for a while now, and this is the first project that ran end-to-end on my RX 7600 XT 16GB.

items.name: Plasma Bigscreen
items.summary: Linux TV interface; a mini-PC user loves phone control through KDE Connect.
items.why_included: A recent home-theater installation earns direct praise for ease of use.
items.evidence: A user installed Plasma Bigscreen on a cheap mini-HTPC, used KDE Connect as a phone remote, and found it easier and preferable to Android TV.

evidence_sources.author: brnt
evidence_sources.excerpt: A week ago I bought a cheap mini-htpc and put Plasma Bigscreen on it, using a phone with KDEconnect as remote. So easy to use! So much better than AndroidTV let alone proprietary crap.

items.name: Navidrome
items.source_story_title: How Not to Build a Music Player
items.summary: Self-hosted music server; smart playlists underpin a listener's offline music routine.
items.why_included: An actual listening workflow gives the recommendation practical specificity.
items.evidence: A listener endorses Navidrome smart playlists with Substreamer or DSub as a great local-music setup, highlighting offline playlist syncing.

evidence_sources.author: sandreas
evidence_sources.excerpt: for music I found navidrome with smart playlists[2] and Substreamer[3] / DSub[4] to be a great way to listen to local music, since Substreamer supports OFFLINE sync for playlists.

items.name: Substreamer
items.source_story_title: How Not to Build a Music Player
items.summary: Music-server client praised for syncing smart playlists for offline listening.
items.why_included: Explicit first-hand praise identifies offline playlist sync as the useful feature.
items.evidence: A listener praises Substreamer in their Navidrome setup because it supports offline playlist syncing.

evidence_sources.author: sandreas
evidence_sources.excerpt: for music I found navidrome with smart playlists[2] and Substreamer[3] / DSub[4] to be a great way to listen to local music, since Substreamer supports OFFLINE sync for playlists.

items.name: Symfonium
items.source_story_title: How Not to Build a Music Player
items.summary: Android music player recommended for Plex libraries and automatic DJ playlists.
items.why_included: A direct recommendation points to a specific Plex music-player alternative.
items.evidence: A commenter explicitly recommends the Android app, spelling it Symphonium, and praises its Plex connection, Smart Flow playlists, and appearance; the official product is Symfonium.

evidence_sources.author: sourweasel
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you're on Android, I highly recommend trying the app Symphonium. It can connect to your Plex music library and the "Smart Flow" playlist bring all the auto DJ modes from Plex amp and add a few more options. It also looks far better imho.

items.name: Auxio
items.source_story_title: How Not to Build a Music Player
items.summary: Android music player praised for tagged libraries and reshuffling on demand.
items.why_included: A first-hand endorsement names concrete library-handling and shuffle behavior.
items.evidence: A commenter says Auxio is excellent for well-tagged libraries and creates a new shuffle order whenever its shuffle button is clicked.

evidence_sources.author: Springtime
evidence_sources.excerpt: Auxio music player[1] for Android shuffles a new order each time the shuffle button is clicked (and ime is excellent for handling well-tagged libraries).

items.name: CultRepo
items.summary: Free software-history documentaries; a viewer particularly recommends the Java film.
items.why_included: A viewer explicitly recommends the catalogue and singles out a film they enjoyed.
items.evidence: A fan recommends CultRepo's free documentary catalogue and particularly enjoyed the Java film's treatment of the Sun and Oracle eras.

evidence_sources.author: vlowrian
evidence_sources.excerpt: I particularly enjoyed the Java documentary, which offered fascinating insights into the differences between the Sun and Oracle eras, many of which I never would have expected.

items.name: How Brains Learn
items.source_story_title: A visual explanation of reinforcement learning
items.summary: Interactive reinforcement-learning explainer praised for its clear, helpful visualization.
items.why_included: An independent reader explicitly praises the explanation rather than merely linking it.
items.evidence: A reader calls the visualization helpful and clear.

evidence_sources.author: bobosha
evidence_sources.excerpt: Love it! It's a very helpful and clear visualization.
